# Business Process Engine
Feature: wfx-erp-product-process · Owner: Varun Kumar (VP - Technology)
Functional Specification for the development team, generated from the finished, product-team-approved Product Mock Studio screens (feature library wfx-erp-product-process). The mock is intentionally lenient; this specification is not — it is the contract the development team builds from, and it goes to QA and then to live sproduction. Items marked ASSUMED are pending product-team sign-off (Section 8).

## Overview

### Purpose
A Business Process Engine (BPE) is a named chain that ties several ERP transactions together in a fixed order — for example a chain named “Order to Ship” whose steps are Sales Order → Packing List → Shipment. This feature lets a business administrator define, name, sequence, activate and retire these chains. Each step is one Document Type (transaction) plus its Sequence position.

### Who uses it
• Business administrators / process owners — create and maintain chains, sequence the transactions, activate and retire them.
• Downstream modules — read the active chain definitions to know which transaction follows which (enforcement/execution is out of scope here; see Section 7 and Q-8).

### Where it sits in the ERP
The feature lives in a new Process module (real target: libs/angular/features/wfx-erp/wfx-erp-process, route /process; the mock library wfx-erp-product-process drops its -product segment on promotion). A BPE is company/tenant-scoped: each chain belongs to a company and its name is unique within that company (D-2, V-1, Q-2).
Scope of this spec: the Business Process Engine LIST screen and the DETAIL (create/edit) screen, including their shared workflow, data contract, and validations. Actually running or enforcing a chain at transaction time is NOT part of this feature (config-only — Q-8).

## Screen inventory & navigation flow

[TABLE 1: Table 1 · 3 rows · columns: # (text), Screen (text), Route (text), Purpose (text)]
| # | Screen | Route | Purpose |
| S-1 | Business Process Engine List | /process/engines | Search, filter and manage all chains; entry point of the feature. /process redirects here. |
| S-2 | Detail — New | /process/engines/new | Create a chain. The record is inserted automatically once the Name (seed field) is filled (auto-save; no Save button). |
| S-3 | Detail — Edit | /process/engines/{id} | View and edit a chain: header fields + the inline-editable steps grid; manual Activate action. |

### Navigation rules
• List → Detail (edit): click the name link in the Process Engine column, or right-click a row and choose Edit. Both open /process/engines/{id}.
• List → Detail (new): the “+ Add New Engine” button opens /process/engines/new.
• Detail → List: the back arrow returns to /process/engines. Any pending auto-save is flushed before navigating away — a navigation must never silently drop an unsaved change.
• Unknown id: error toast “That process engine does not exist.” and the user is returned to the list.
• Browser/page titles: “Business Process Engines” (list), “New Business Process Engine” (new), “Business Process Engine” (edit).
• Back-navigation state: the mock does not preserve list state (filters, page). The real screen must restore search, filters, sort and page exactly as the user left it (QA checklist §5) — Q-11.

## Conventions
Rules referenced throughout the field tables and the Validations master list are defined once here, so no field restates them.

[TABLE 2: Table 2 · 5 rows · columns: Convention (text), Definition (text) · identifiers: Convention]
| Convention | Definition |
| Enforcement | The server enforces every rule; client validation is a convenience, not the enforcement. |
| Seed fields | Name. A new process engine is created once Name is valid. |
| Text fields | Trimmed; a mandatory text field must contain at least one non-whitespace character; length hard-stops at the stated maximum. |
| Company scope | A BPE is company/tenant-scoped: the list is filtered to the current company and name-uniqueness is enforced within it (V-1). |
| Date display | All dates display via the app-wide WfxDateFormatService (user preference, default dd MMM yyyy) — never a hardcoded locale. |

## Screen specifications

### Business Process Engine List (S-1)
Purpose: single working list of all chains with search, a status filter, bulk selection, row actions and navigation into the detail screen.
Business Process Engine List — light mode, Team Data

#### Layout
• Page header: breadcrumb “Process”, title “Business Process Engines”, subtitle, and a primary “+ Add New Engine” button.
• Content toolbar: quick-search input (“Search by name or description”) and a clearable, searchable Status dropdown.
• Grid inside a surface card; floating filter row pinned under the headers; pagination footer always visible.
• Floating selection bar appears when rows are selected, with the count, a Clear action and a Delete action.

#### Toolbar behaviours
• Quick search matches Name (BPEName) OR Description, case-insensitive substring, trimmed. Real build: debounce 300 ms.
• Status dropdown filters to exactly one status; clearable (shows all). Values: Draft, Active, Inactive.
• Toolbar filter and in-grid column filters combine (logical AND).

#### Grid specification

[TABLE 3: Table 3 · 7 rows · columns: Column (text), Content & combined cells (text), Filter (text), Format / behaviour (text) · identifiers: Column]
| Column | Content & combined cells | Filter | Format / behaviour |
| (selection) | Row checkbox + header checkbox | — | Multi-row selection; header checkbox selects the filtered set only. |
| Status | wfx-badge chip, never plain text | Set filter (Draft, Active, Inactive; fixed order) | Severity: Draft = secondary (grey), Active = success (green), Inactive = warning (amber). |
| Process Engine | Combined cell — Name (link, opens detail) over Description (secondary line) | Text filter | Link via data-action="open-bpe" + onCellClicked; autoHeight on. Blank cell renders “—”. |
| Applicability | Combined cell — dimension label (primary) over the chosen value names (secondary) | Set filter (by dimension) | autoHeight on. A blank rule renders “All”; a dimension with no values renders “(no values)”. Read-only here (set on the detail). |
| Steps | Step count (StepCount) | Number filter | Right-aligned; formatted “N step(s)”; zero renders “—”. See F-1 (incomplete steps still counted). |
| Created By | Name of the user who created the chain (CreatedBy) | Set filter | Avatar chip + name via WfxUserGroupCellRendererComponent; autoHeight on; blank renders “—”. Mock stamps a fixed current user (no login); real takes it from the session (D-5). |
| Created On | Creation date | Date (equals / before / after / from–to) | App-wide date format via WfxDateFormatService (default dd MMM yyyy). Calendar picker; filtering by a day matches any time on that day. |
• Default column config: resizable, sortable, floating filter row on, min width 90.
• Pagination: page sizes 20 / 50 / 100, default 20. Default sort: Created On descending (ASSUMED — Q-11).
• Row model: the mock grid is client-side. The real list must use the server-side row model with server paging/sort/filter (D-3).
• Actions: the mock exposes row actions only through the right-click context menu. The real screen must additionally provide a pinned-right actions (kebab) column with the same items — right-click alone is not discoverable (F-2).

#### Row actions (context menu)
Row context menu on a Draft chain (Team Data)

[TABLE 4: Table 4 · 4 rows · columns: Action (text), Shown when (text), Behaviour (text) · identifiers: Action]
| Action | Shown when | Behaviour |
| Edit | Always | Opens the detail screen for the row. |
| Activate | Status ≠ Active | Guard: needs ≥ 2 steps (else warning M-4). Confirmation dialog, then Status = Active. |
| Set Inactive | Status = Active | Opens the Set Inactive dialog; reason is mandatory (stored in Comments in the mock — D-11). |
| Delete | Status = Draft or Inactive | Confirmation dialog, then hard delete. Active rows are not deletable (M-13). |

#### Bulk actions
• Selecting rows shows the floating selection bar with the count and a Delete button.
• Bulk delete first validates every selected row against the delete rule; if any row is Active the whole action is blocked with a warning naming the blocked chains — nothing is partially deleted.
• After a successful bulk delete the selection is cleared and the list reloads.

#### Set Inactive dialog
• Modal, header “Set Process Engine Inactive”, helper text “Enter a reason to set this process engine inactive.”, one required Reason textarea (4 rows), buttons OK (primary) / Close.
• OK with a blank/whitespace reason shows warning “Reason is mandatory.” and keeps the dialog open.
• OK with a reason sets Status = Inactive and stores the reason. Real build: store it in a dedicated field with an audit entry (who/when); it must not double as free-text Comments (D-11, Q-7).

#### Empty, loading and error states
• Empty list: grid shows its no-rows overlay. Real build: message “No process engines found” with an Add New Engine call to action (ASSUMED — Q-12).
• Load failure: error toast “Load Failed — Could not load process engines.”; the grid stays empty, never silently blank.

### Business Process Engine Detail (S-2 / S-3)
Purpose: create and edit a chain. There is NO Save button — the screen auto-saves (see Auto-save behaviour). Activate is the only manual action.
Detail — existing chain (Team Data): Engine Details + editable Chain Steps grid
Detail — new chain (Add Step disabled until the Name is saved)

#### Layout
• Page header: breadcrumbs “Process › Business Process Engines”, back arrow, title “Add Process Engine” (new) or “Process Engine — {BPEName}” (existing), save-status indicator, a Status badge (once the record exists), and the Activate button.
• Two panels: Engine Details (Name, Description) and Chain Steps (the editable grid + “+ Add Step”).

#### Field table — Engine Details

[TABLE 5: Table 5 · 2 rows · columns: Field (text), Type (text), Required (text), Validation (text), Default (text), Source / DDL (text)]
| Field | Type | Required | Validation | Default | Source / DDL |
| Name | Text input | Yes (seed) | V-1 (max 120, not blank, unique within company) | empty | Free text |
| Description | Textarea (2 rows) | No | V-2 (max 500) | empty | Free text |

#### Applicability rule
An optional rule that scopes WHICH entities the chain applies to. It is one dimension (single-select) plus its values (multi-select). Leave it blank to apply to everything (the list shows “All”). One rule per chain for now (Q-13).

[TABLE 6: Table 6 · 2 rows · columns: Field (text), Type (text), Required (boolean), Options (text), Default (text), Source / DDL (text)]
| Field | Type | Required | Options | Default | Source / DDL |
| Applies To (dimension) | Single-select (clearable) | No | Company, Buyer Type, Buyer, Category | none (= All) | Fixed dimension list |
| Values | Multi-select (chips) | No | Depend on the chosen dimension (Company: WFX India/Bangladesh/Vietnam; Buyer Type: Direct/Agent/Buying House/Licensee; Buyer: buyer master; Category: product-category master) | none | Per-dimension master/DDL (D-12, Q-1) |
• Changing the dimension clears any previously-picked values.
• The Values control is disabled until a dimension is chosen.
• Editable on both the New and Edit form; auto-saves like the rest of the screen.
• Stored as ApplicabilityDimension (code) + ApplicabilityDimensionName (label) + ApplicabilityValues (array of {Code, Name}).

#### Chain Steps grid (inline-editable)
Chain Steps — inline Document Type dropdown (single-click to edit)

[TABLE 7: Table 7 · 2 rows · columns: Column (text), Editor (text), Validation (text), Behaviour (text)]
| Column | Editor | Validation | Behaviour |
| Sequence | Number cell editor (min 1, 0 decimals) | V-3 | Right-aligned; dashed-border editable cell. On add, auto-fills as max(existing)+1. |
| Document Type (Transaction) | Single-select cell editor | V-4, V-5 | Stores the transaction code, displays the label. Options from the transaction-type DDL (mock: 9 static values — D-4, Q-1). |
• “+ Add Step” (panel header) appends a new row with the next sequence; disabled until the record exists (Name saved). New-record guard message M-14.
• Editing is single-click; the select overlay is body-appended so it is never clipped. Each edit auto-saves the chain (the whole Steps array — D-1, D-10).
• On an invalid inline edit the cell reverts to its previous value and a warning toast explains why (M-15/M-16/M-17).
• Remove a step via right-click → “Remove step”. Real build: add a confirmation before removal (F-3).
• Documented transactions (mock list): Sales Order (OC), Purchase Order, Fabric/Trims Store-In (GRN), Cutting, Sewing / Production, Finishing, Packing List, Shipment (ASN/GDN), Sales Invoice.

#### Auto-save behaviour
• Seed field (must be filled before the record is created): Name. Description and steps are not seed fields.
• New chain: the record is inserted automatically the moment Name is valid; Status = Draft. Only then does Add Step enable.
• Existing chain: every change (header fields OR steps) is debounce-saved automatically. The mock PUTs the whole record; the real screen PATCHes header fields and does per-step CRUD (D-10).
• The save-status indicator shows idle → saving → saved / error. A failed save shows toast “Save Failed — Could not save the process engine.” and stays in error until a later save succeeds.
• Loaded values never count as dirty — opening a chain must not trigger a save.

#### Activate action
Activate confirmation dialog
• Activate is visible for any existing (already auto-saved) chain — including one already Active (re-activate after an edit; per the product decision an edited Active chain stays Active — T-3, Q-3).
• Activate gate: form valid, ≥ 2 steps (V-6), and every step has a Document Type (V-4). Failures show M-6 / M-7 / M-8.
• First activate dialog: title “Activate Process Engine”, text “Activate {BPEName}? It becomes available to run as a chain (it can be set Inactive later, with a reason, from the list).” Yes/No.
• Re-activate dialog: title “Re-activate Process Engine”, text “Save and re-activate the current changes to {BPEName}?”.
• On success: Status = Active, success toast “{BPEName} is now active.”, header badge refreshes, list reflects the change on return.

#### Alerts & messages (exact wording)

| # | Trigger | Kind | Title | Message |

| M-6 | Activate (detail) with invalid form | Warning toast | Validation | Please fix the highlighted fields before activating. |
| M-7 | Activate (detail), < 2 steps | Warning toast | Not Enough Steps | A process engine needs at least 2 steps before it can be activated. |
| M-8 | Activate (detail), a step lacks a Document Type | Warning toast | Incomplete Step | Every step must have a Document Type before activating. |
| M-9 | Activate (detail) confirm | Confirm dialog | Activate Process Engine | Activate {BPEName}? It becomes available to run as a chain (it can be set Inactive later, with a reason, from the list). |

| M-14 | Add Step before the chain is saved | Warning toast | Enter a Name first | Give the process engine a name before adding steps. |
| M-15 | Inline: invalid sequence | Warning toast | Not Allowed | Sequence must be a whole number of 1 or more. |
| M-16 | Inline: duplicate sequence | Warning toast | Not Allowed | Sequence {n} is already used by another step. |
| M-17 | Inline: duplicate transaction | Warning toast | Not Allowed | That transaction is already in this chain. |
| M-18 | Delete confirm | Confirm dialog | Confirm Delete | Delete {BPEName}? This cannot be undone. |
| M-19 | Delete succeeded | Success toast | Deleted | {BPEName} was deleted. |
| M-20 | Bulk delete with blocked (Active) rows | Warning toast | Not Allowed | {n} of the selected chain(s) are Active and cannot be deleted ({names}). Deselect them and try again. |
| M-21 | Detail: unknown id | Error toast | Not Found | That process engine does not exist. |
| M-22 | Auto-save failed | Error toast | Save Failed | Could not save the process engine. |
| M-23 | Duplicate name (inline field error) | Inline error | — | A process engine with this name already exists |

## Workflow & status lifecycle

[TABLE 9: Table 9 · 3 rows · columns: Status (text), Badge severity (text), Meaning (text)]
| Status | Badge severity | Meaning |
| Draft | Secondary (grey) | Auto-saved draft; fully editable; deletable; not yet usable as a chain. |
| Active | Success (green) | Published and available to run as a chain; not deletable; stays editable (edits keep it Active — Q-3). |
| Inactive | Warning (amber) | Retired with a mandatory reason; editable; deletable; can be re-activated. |

### Allowed transitions

[TABLE 10: Table 10 · 6 rows · columns: # (text), Transition (text), Trigger (text), Who / where (text) · identifiers: #]
| # | Transition | Trigger | Who / where |
| T-1 | (new) → Draft | Automatic: Name filled → record inserted | Auto-save engine, detail screen |
| T-2 | Draft → Active | Manual Activate + confirm (M-9); gate: ≥ 2 steps, all steps complete, form valid | Detail toolbar; list context menu |
| T-3 | Active → Active (edited) | Edit then Re-activate (M-10). Per product decision, editing an Active chain keeps it Active (no versioning) | Detail screen. Real: re-validate on save — F-5, Q-3 |
| T-4 | Active → Inactive | Manual Set Inactive + mandatory reason | List context menu |
| T-5 | Inactive → Active | Manual Activate (same gate as T-2) | List context menu / detail |
| T-6 | Draft / Inactive → (deleted) | Manual Delete + confirm (M-18) | List context menu / bulk bar |
• An Active chain may never be hard-deleted — set it Inactive (with a reason) first.
• Irreversible actions (Delete) always use a confirmation dialog that spells out the impact.
• Server is the source of truth: it must re-validate every transition (never trust the client).

## Validations master list
One line per field — its checks combined; shared rules are defined once under Conventions. Every rule is testable as written; inline messages show at the field, toasts per Section 3.

[TABLE 11: Table 11 · 9 rows · columns: # (text), Rule (testable statement) (text), Where enforced (text), Message (text) · identifiers: #]
| # | Rule (testable statement) | Where enforced | Message |
| V-1 | Name — required (seed); trimmed, not blank; &le; 120 chars (input hard-stops at 120); unique within the company (case-insensitive, trimmed). | Detail form + server | Name is required / cannot be blank / A process engine with this name already exists |
| V-2 | Description — &le; 500 chars. | Detail form + server | — |
| V-3 | Step Sequence — whole number &ge; 1; unique within the chain (no two steps share a number); gaps allowed (Q-5). | Steps grid + server | Sequence must be a whole number of 1 or more. / Sequence {n} is already used by another step. |
| V-4 | Each step must have a Document Type before the chain can be Activated. | Detail (activate gate) + server | Every step must have a Document Type before activating. |
| V-5 | A Document Type may appear at most once per chain (no transaction twice). | Steps grid + server | That transaction is already in this chain. |
| V-6 | A chain needs at least 2 steps to be Activated. | Detail + list + server | A process engine needs at least 2 steps before it can be activated. |
| V-7 | Activate is blocked while the form is invalid. | Detail | Please fix the highlighted fields before activating. |
| V-8 | Delete is allowed only when Status is Draft or Inactive. | List + server | {BPEName} is Active and cannot be deleted. Set it Inactive (with a reason) first. |
| V-9 | Set Inactive requires a non-blank reason. | List dialog + server | Reason is mandatory. |

## Out-of-scope & deltas

### Mock shortcuts (real behaviour the dev team must implement)

[TABLE 12: Table 12 · 9 rows · columns: # (text), Mock shortcut (text), Real behaviour required (text) · identifiers: #]
| # | Mock shortcut | Real behaviour required |
| D-1 | Steps are embedded as a Steps array on the engine record; the whole record is saved as one unit. | Split into header (xtBPEMain) + lines (xtBPEStep) tables with a BPEID foreign key; steps get their own create/update/delete endpoints. |
| D-2 | No company/tenant field; a single flat list. | A BPE is company/tenant-scoped: add CompanyCode/TenantID (from session), filter the list to the current company, and enforce name-uniqueness within the company (V-1). Q-2. |
| D-3 | Client-side grid over the full list. | Server-side row model with server paging, sorting and filtering from day one. |
| D-4 | Document Type list is 9 static values in code. | Source the transaction-type list from the DDL/master API; the authoritative set and labels are Q-1. |
| D-5 | CreatedOn is tracked, and Created By is shown in the list (CreatedBy) — but the mock stamps a fixed user name since there is no login. | Take Created By from the authenticated session/JWT; add ModifiedBy / ModifiedOn (and store an id, not just a display name). Q-7. |
| D-10 | Every change PUTs the whole record. | PATCH only the dirty header fields; persist step changes through the step endpoints (D-1). |
| D-11 | The Set Inactive reason is stored in the free-text Comments field. | Store the reason in a dedicated field with an audit entry (who/when); do not overload a general Comments field. Q-7. |
| D-6 | The screen only defines chains. | Actually running/enforcing a chain at transaction time is a separate feature and is out of scope here. Confirm where enforcement lives — Q-8. |
| D-12 | The Applicability value lists (companies, buyer types, buyers, categories) are static in the mock. | Source each dimension’s values from its master/DDL (company master, buyer-type DDL, buyer master, product-category master). Q-1. |

### Findings (fix in the real build)

[TABLE 13: Table 13 · 5 rows · columns: # (text), Finding (text), Corrected rule for the real build (text) · identifiers: #]
| # | Finding | Corrected rule for the real build |
| F-1 | An incomplete step (added but no Document Type picked) is auto-saved and counted in StepCount, so the list can show “3 steps” where one is blank. | Do not persist an incomplete step (or exclude it from StepCount); a chain shows only its complete steps. Activate already blocks incomplete steps (V-4). |
| F-2 | List row actions are reachable only by right-click (no visible actions column). | Add a pinned-right kebab actions column with the same items; right-click stays as a shortcut (grid standard). |
| F-3 | “Remove step” deletes the row immediately with no confirmation (every other destructive action confirms). | Confirm step removal before deleting. |
| F-4 — FIXED in the mock | The list Created On column used a text filter, which matched the raw ISO value instead of the shown date. It now declares cellDataType: 'dateString' + filter: 'agDateColumnFilter'. | Use a date filter for the date column (grid standard) — equals / before / after / from–to on a calendar picker. Build the real screen this way. |
| F-5 | Editing an Active chain is not re-validated — a user can remove steps below 2, or leave a step incomplete, while the chain stays Active. | Re-validate an Active chain on every save; if an edit makes it invalid, block the save (or drop it to Draft) with a clear message. Exact behaviour Q-3. |

[TABLE 14: Table 14 · 13 rows · columns: # (text), Question (text), Proposed default (text), Owner (text) · identifiers: #]
| # | Question | Proposed default | Owner |
| Q-1 | What is the authoritative Document Type / transaction list and which DDL/master feeds it? (mock uses 9 representative values) | Source from the transaction-type DDL; treat the mock 9 as representative until confirmed. | Product owner |
| Q-2 | Company/tenant scoping: is the company taken from the logged-in session, and is name-uniqueness per company? Field name? | Company from session; name unique within company; field CompanyCode. | Product owner |
| Q-3 | Editing an Active chain: it stays Active (decided) — but when an edit makes it invalid (< 2 steps / incomplete step), block the save, or drop to Draft? | Block the save with a message; keep it Active. | Product owner |
| Q-4 | Max lengths: Name 120, Description 500 — match the real DB column sizes? | Keep 120 / 500 unless the DB differs. | Product owner |
| Q-5 | Sequence gaps allowed (1, 3, 5), or force contiguous and auto-renumber on removal? | Allow gaps; any unique positive whole number. | Product owner |
| Q-6 | Is there a maximum number of steps per chain? | No hard maximum. | Product owner |
| Q-7 | Audit & the Inactive reason: track CreatedBy/ModifiedBy/ModifiedOn, and store the Inactive reason in its own field? | Yes to both. | Product owner |
| Q-8 | Where is a chain actually enforced/executed at transaction time (this screen is config-only)? | Separate feature; out of scope for this spec. | Product owner |
| Q-9 | Can a chain move directly Inactive → Active, and does Draft ever need a reason to change? | Inactive → Active allowed (same gate); Draft transitions need no reason. | Product owner |
| Q-10 | Should two different chains be allowed to contain the same transaction? (uniqueness is per-chain only) | Yes — uniqueness is only within a single chain. | Product owner |
| Q-11 | List default sort, page size, and preserved back-navigation state? | Created On descending; page 20; restore filters/sort/page on back. | Product owner |
| Q-12 | Empty-state message + call to action for the list? | “No process engines found” + Add New Engine. | Product owner |
| Q-13 | Applicability: one rule per chain for now (one dimension + values). Will this grow to several rules / combined dimensions (e.g. Buyer AND Category), and should a chosen dimension require at least one value? | One rule for now; may extend later; values optional (blank dimension = All). | Product owner |

## Technical appendix — Data & API contract provisional
The committed mock JSON (mock-data/wfx-erp-product-business-process-engines.mock.json) is the draft API contract. Field names are PascalCase DTO names. A real backend would split the header from the lines into two tables (see D-1) and add company-scope + audit columns (D-2, D-5); reconcile field-by-field during promotion.

### Engine (header) record

[TABLE 15: Table 15 · 15 rows · columns: Field (text), Type (text), Example (text), Read by (text), Written by (text) · identifiers: Field]
| Field | Type | Example | Read by | Written by |
| id | string (UUID) | c46de729-… | Both screens (row id, routing) | Server on insert (mock: client UUID) |
| BPEID | number (header PK) | 1001 | — (carried for the real API) | Server |
| BPEName | string (≤120) | Order to Ship | List (Process Engine column), Detail (title), messages | Detail (seed field) |
| Description | string (≤500) | Full flow from order to shipment | List (secondary line), Detail | Detail |
| Status | enum: Draft | Active | Inactive | Active | List (badge, filter), Detail (badge, Activate logic) | Lifecycle actions only — never a free edit |
| ApplicabilityDimension | string (Company | BuyerType | Buyer | Category | '') | Buyer | List (Applicability), Detail (Applies To) | Detail (blank = All) |
| ApplicabilityDimensionName | string | Buyer | List (Applicability primary) | Derived from the dimension on save |
| ApplicabilityValues | array<{ Code, Name }> | [{Code:'BUY001',Name:'Acme Retail Group'}] | List (Applicability secondary), Detail (Values) | Detail (multi-select). Real: values from the per-dimension master (D-12) |
| Steps | array<Step> (embedded in the mock) | see below | Detail (grid), List (StepCount) | Detail (steps grid). Real: own table (D-1) |
| StepCount | number | 3 | List (Steps column) | Derived on save. Real: count only complete steps (F-1) |
| Comments | string | retired — superseded | — | Set Inactive reason (mock reuses this field — D-11) |

CANDIDATES FOR REVIEW (possible definitions, formulas, validations, steps; not confirmed knowledge)
- definition (§ Business Process Engine): The mock is intentionally lenient; this specification is not — it is the contract the development team builds from, and it goes to QA and then to live sproduction.
- definition (§ Business Process Engine): Items marked ASSUMED are pending product-team sign-off (Section 8).
- definition (§ Business Process Engine › Overview › Purpose): A Business Process Engine (BPE) is a named chain that ties several ERP transactions together in a fixed order — for example a chain named “Order to Ship” whose steps are Sales Order → Packing List → Shipment.
- definition (§ Business Process Engine › Overview › Purpose): Each step is one Document Type (transaction) plus its Sequence position.
- definition (§ Business Process Engine › Overview › Where it sits in the ERP): A BPE is company/tenant-scoped: each chain belongs to a company and its name is unique within that company (D-2, V-1, Q-2).
- definition (§ Business Process Engine › Overview › Where it sits in the ERP): Actually running or enforcing a chain at transaction time is NOT part of this feature (config-only — Q-8).
- table (§ Business Process Engine › Screen inventory & navigation flow, table 1): Table 1: #, Screen, Route, Purpose (3 rows)
- definition (§ Business Process Engine › Screen inventory & navigation flow › Navigation rules): Any pending auto-save is flushed before navigating away — a navigation must never silently drop an unsaved change.
- validation (§ Business Process Engine › Screen inventory & navigation flow › Navigation rules): Any pending auto-save is flushed before navigating away — a navigation must never silently drop an unsaved change.
- validation (§ Business Process Engine › Screen inventory & navigation flow › Navigation rules): The real screen must restore search, filters, sort and page exactly as the user left it (QA checklist §5) — Q-11.
- workflow_steps (§ Business Process Engine › Screen inventory & navigation flow › Navigation rules): Navigation rules: / 1. List → Detail (edit): click the name link in the Process Engine column, or right-click a row and choose Edit. Both open /process/engines/{id}. / 2. List → Detail (new): the “+ Add New Engine” button opens /process/engines/new. / 3. Detail → List: the back arrow returns to /process/engines. Any pending auto-save is flushed before navigating away — a navigation must never silently drop an unsaved change. / 4. Unknown id: error toast “That process engine does not exist.” and the user is returned to the list. / 5. Browser/page titles: “Business Process Engines” (list), “New Business Process Engine” (new), “Business Process Engine” (edit). / 6. Back-navigation state: the mock does not preserve list state (filters, page). The real screen must restore search, filters, sort and page exactly as the user left it (QA checklist §5) — Q-11.

- formula (§ Business Process Engine › Screen specifications › Business Process Engine Detail (S-2 / S-3) › Auto-save behaviour): New chain: the record is inserted automatically the moment Name is valid; Status = Draft.
- validation (§ Business Process Engine › Screen specifications › Business Process Engine Detail (S-2 / S-3) › Auto-save behaviour): Loaded values never count as dirty — opening a chain must not trigger a save.
- workflow_steps (§ Business Process Engine › Screen specifications › Business Process Engine Detail (S-2 / S-3) › Auto-save behaviour): Auto-save behaviour: / 1. Seed field (must be filled before the record is created): Name. Description and steps are not seed fields. / 2. New chain: the record is inserted automatically the moment Name is valid; Status = Draft. Only then does Add Step enable. / 3. Existing chain: every change (header fields OR steps) is debounce-saved automatically. The mock PUTs the whole record; the real screen PATCHes header fields and does per-step CRUD (D-10). / 4. The save-status indicator shows idle → saving → saved / error. A failed save shows toast “Save Failed — Could not save the process engine.” and stays in error until a later save succeeds. / 5. Loaded values never count as dirty — opening a chain must not trigger a save.
- definition (§ Business Process Engine › Screen specifications › Business Process Engine Detail (S-2 / S-3) › Activate action): Activate is visible for any existing (already auto-saved) chain — including one already Active (re-activate after an edit; per the product decision an edited Active chain stays Active — T-3, Q-3).
- formula (§ Business Process Engine › Screen specifications › Business Process Engine Detail (S-2 / S-3) › Activate action): On success: Status = Active, success toast “{BPEName} is now active.”, header badge refreshes, list reflects the change on return.
- workflow_steps (§ Business Process Engine › Screen specifications › Business Process Engine Detail (S-2 / S-3) › Activate action): Activate action: / 1. Activate is visible for any existing (already auto-saved) chain — including one already Active (re-activate after an edit; per the product decision an edited Active chain stays Active — T-3, Q-3). / 2. Activate gate: form valid, ≥ 2 steps (V-6), and every step has a Document Type (V-4). Failures show M-6 / M-7 / M-8. / 3. First activate dialog: title “Activate Process Engine”, text “Activate {BPEName}? It becomes available to run as a chain (it can be set Inactive later, with a reason, from the list).” Yes/No. / 4. Re-activate dialog: title “Re-activate Process Engine”, text “Save and re-activate the current changes to {BPEName}?”. / 5. On success: Status = Active, success toast “{BPEName} is now active.”, header badge refreshes, list reflects the change on return.
